name: agentmako

hlido_opinion.headline: A local-first MCP server that gives coding agents a live, queryable map of your repo — a broad typed-tool surface and a durable 'findings' layer, from a small but Apache-licensed project.
hlido_opinion.body: agentmako is a local-first MCP server that keeps a project's code, routes, schema, diagnostics, rules, findings and freshness state queryable for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Cline and other MCP clients. Its distinctive idea is the Reef engine — not just an index, but a durable fact-and-finding layer that remembers what changed, what failed, what was reviewed, and whether a piece of evidence is fresh enough for an agent to trust, with a background daemon that watches edits and refreshes the map. The tool surface is unusually broad for a young project: two dozen typed tools spanning context packets, AST pattern search, route tracing, import-impact analysis, database schema and RLS inspection, a tenant-leak audit, git pre-commit checks, and project-convention extraction. Several of those (RLS inspection, tenant-leak audit) point at a genuinely useful multi-tenant-security angle most codebase tools ignore. The honesty markers are good — 'local-first, no hosted service', 'node >= 20', 'apache-2.0', typed tools — so there is no cloud dependency to trust and the license is permissive. What holds it to the lower-middle of STEADY is maturity and proof: 51 GitHub stars, no published benchmarks or independent evidence for the Reef 'freshness' claims, and a large tool surface whose reliability across real repos the public page asserts rather than demonstrates. It is a promising, well-scoped local server; it is early, and it is honest about being early.

tier_rationale: STEADY (74), lower-middle, because agentmako is a genuinely agent-native, local-first, Apache-licensed MCP server with a broad typed-tool surface and a thoughtful durable-findings layer (Reef), including rare multi-tenant-security tooling. It sits low in the band because it is early (51 stars), publishes no benchmarks or independent evidence for its freshness/durability claims, and its broad tool surface is asserted rather than demonstrated reliable across real projects.
what_it_does_well: Local-first with no hosted service — code and queries stay on your machine
Reef engine adds a durable fact-and-finding layer that survives across sessions, not just a static index
Broad typed-tool surface (~two dozen) covering context, AST search, route tracing, import impact and more
Rare multi-tenant-security tooling: RLS inspection and a tenant-leak audit
Background daemon watches edits and tracks evidence freshness so the agent knows what to trust
Apache-2.0 licensed and node >= 20 — permissive and low-dependency
Works across Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor and Cline
what_it_fails_at: Early-stage traction — around 51 GitHub stars at review
No published benchmarks or independent evidence for the Reef freshness/durability claims
A large tool surface whose per-tool reliability across real repos is asserted, not demonstrated
Single-maintainer-scale project with no continuity or support signal published
No pricing/support model because it is a free local tool — fine, but no commercial backing either
best_for: Developers who want a local-first, no-cloud MCP map of their repo for a coding agent
Multi-tenant SaaS teams who value the RLS-inspection and tenant-leak-audit tools
Users who prefer an Apache-licensed tool they can run and inspect entirely locally
not_recommended_for: Teams needing a supported, SLA-backed product with a continuity guarantee
Buyers who require published benchmarks before adopting a repo-analysis tool
Anyone wanting a hosted, zero-setup service rather than a local daemon

compared_to.verdict_diff: Serena is a more established semantic code-navigation MCP toolkit; agentmako adds a durable findings layer (Reef) and multi-tenant-security tools but is earlier and less proven. Serena for maturity, agentmako for its findings-persistence idea and security-focused tools.

Neo4j's MCP server exposes a graph database you model; agentmako is a purpose-built local repo map with typed code tools. Neo4j's for general graph data, agentmako for out-of-the-box, local codebase context.

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: A local-first MCP server. An agent connects agentmako to a project ('agentmako connect .') and calls typed tools — context_packet, ast_find_pattern, route_trace, imports_impact, db_rls, tenant_leak_audit, git_precommit_check and more — to get structured repo context and durable findings. Works with Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor and Cline. Runs entirely locally with no API key.
